arxiv-1702-08703.title: Widely-Linear Precoding for Large-Scale MIMO with IQI: Algorithms and Performance Analysis W. Zhang is with Jiangsu University, China. He was with CETUC, PUC-Rio, Brazil. (e-mail:wencezhang@ujs.edu.cn) R. C. de Lamare is with the University of York, UK, and PUC-Rio, Brazil. (e-mail:delamare@cetuc.pu
arxiv-1702-08703.creator: Wence Zhang, Rodrigo C. de Lamare, , Cunhua Pan, Ming Chen, Jianxin Dai, Bingyang Wu and Xu Bao
arxiv-1702-08703.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Wence Zhang, Rodrigo C. de Lamare, , Cunhua Pan, Ming Chen, Jianxin Dai, Bingyang Wu and Xu Bao. In this paper we study widely-linear precoding techniques to mitigate in-phase/quadrature-phase (IQ) imbalance (IQI) in the downlink of large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. We adopt a real-valued signal model which takes into account the IQI at the transmitter and then develop widely-linear zero-forcing (WL-ZF), widely-linear matched filter (WL-MF), widely-linear minimum mean-squared error (WL-MMSE) and widely-linear block-diagonalization (WL-BD) type precoding algorithms for both single- and multiple-antenna users.

arxiv-2012-06124.title: Universal quantum gates, artificial neurons and pattern recognition simulated by LC resonators
arxiv-2012-06124.creator: Motohiko Ezawa
arxiv-2012-06124.description: Abstract We propose to simulate quantum gates by LC resonators, where the amplitude and the phase of the voltage describe the quantum state. By controlling capacitance or inductance of resonators, it is possible to control the phase of the voltage arbitrarily. A set of resonators acts as the phase-shift, the Hadamard and the CNOT gates.

arxiv-2106-06166.title: Self-Guided Quantum State Learning for Mixed States
arxiv-2106-06166.creator: Ahmad Farooq, Muhammad Asad Ullah, Syahri Ramadhani, Junaid ur Rehman, Hyundong Shin
arxiv-2106-06166.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ahmad Farooq, Muhammad Asad Ullah, Syahri Ramadhani, Junaid ur Rehman, Hyundong Shin. We provide an adaptive learning algorithm for tomography of general quantum states. Our proposal is based on the simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation algorithm and is applicable on mixed qudit states.

arxiv-2303-07889.title: Understanding the Uncertainty Loop of Human-Robot Interaction CCS: Human-centered computing Human computer interaction (HCI) CCS: Computer systems organization Robotics
arxiv-2303-07889.creator: Jan Leusmann, Chao Wang, Michael Gienger, Albrecht Schmidt, Sven Mayer
arxiv-2303-07889.description: Abstract . Recently the field of Human-Robot Interaction gained popularity due to the wide range of possibilities of how robots can support humans during daily tasks. One such form is supportive robots, socially assistive robots built explicitly for communicating with humans, e.g., as service robots or personal companions.

arxiv-2303-08116.title: Optimizing Quantum Federated Learning Based on Federated Quantum Natural Gradient Descent
arxiv-2303-08116.creator: Jun Qi, Xiao-Lei Zhang, Javier Tejedor
arxiv-2303-08116.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jun Qi, Xiao-Lei Zhang, Javier Tejedor. Quantum federated learning (QFL) is a quantum extension of the classical federated learning model across multiple local quantum devices. An efficient optimization algorithm is always expected to minimize the communication overhead among different quantum participants. In this work, we propose an efficient optimization algorithm, namely federated quantum natural gradient descent (FQNGD), and further, apply it to a QFL framework that is composed of a variational quantum circuit (VQC)-based quantum neural networks (QNN).

In this paper, the second coefficient of the normalized analytic function f f defined on the open unit disc is constrained to define new classes of analytic functions.

arxiv-2307-05779.title: Neural Machine Translation Data Generation and Augmentation using ChatGPT
arxiv-2307-05779.creator: Wayne Yang, Garrett Nicolai
arxiv-2307-05779.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wayne Yang, Garrett Nicolai. Neural models have revolutionized the field of machine translation, but creating parallel corpora is expensive and time-consuming. We investigate an alternative to manual parallel corpora - hallucinated parallel corpora created by generative language models. Although these models are themselves trained on parallel data, they can leverage a multilingual vector space to create data, and may be able to supplement small manually-procured corpora.

arxiv-2405-19029.title: Convex neural network synthesis for robustness in the 1-norm
arxiv-2405-19029.creator: Ross Drummond, Chris Guiver, Matthew C. Turner
arxiv-2405-19029.description: Abstract With neural networks being used to control safety-critical systems, they increasingly have to be both accurate (in the sense of matching inputs to outputs) and robust. However, these two properties are often at odds with each other and a trade-off has to be navigated.

arxiv-2407-12620.title: Harnessing the Power of Artificial Intelligence to Vitalize Endangered Indigenous Languages: Technologies and Experiences
arxiv-2407-12620.creator: Claudio Pinhanez, Paulo Cavalin, Luciana Storto, Thomas Finbow, Alexander Cobbinah, Julio Nogima, Marisa Vasconcelos, Pedro Domingues, Priscila de Souza Mizukami, Nicole Grell, Majoí Gongora, Isabel Gonçalves
arxiv-2407-12620.description: Abstract Since 2022 we have been exploring application areas and technologies in which Artificial Intelligence (AI) and modern Natural Language Processing (NLP), such as Large Language Models (LLMs), can be employed to foster the usage and facilitate the documentation of Indigenous languages which are in danger of disappearing.

arxiv-2601-22450.title: Tuning the Implicit Regularizer of Masked Diffusion Language Models: Enhancing Generalization via Insights from k k -Parity
arxiv-2601-22450.creator: Jianhao Huang, Baharan Mirzasoleiman
arxiv-2601-22450.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jianhao Huang, Baharan Mirzasoleiman. Masked Diffusion Language Models have recently emerged as a powerful generative paradigm, yet their generalization properties remain understudied compared to their auto-regressive counterparts. In this work, we investigate these properties within the setting of the k k -parity problem (computing the XOR sum of k k relevant bits), where neural networks typically exhibit grokking—a prolonged plateau of chance-level performance followed by sudden generalization.

arxiv-2602-04769.title: Yan Chen
arxiv-2602-04769.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by *. Accurate and timely seizure detection from Electroencephalography (EEG) is critical for clinical intervention, yet manual review of long-term recordings is labor-intensive. Recent efforts to encode EEG signals into large language models (LLMs) show promise in handling neural signals across diverse patients, but two significant challenges remain: (1) multi-channel heterogeneity , as seizure-relevant information varies substantially across EEG channels, and (2) computing inefficiency , as the EEG signals need to be encoded into a massive number of tokens for the prediction.

arxiv-2602-08273.title: Pitot-Aided Attitude and Air Velocity Estimation with Almost Global Asymptotic Stability Guarantees
arxiv-2602-08273.creator: Méloné Nyoba Tchonkeu, Soulaimane Berkane, Tarek Hamel
arxiv-2602-08273.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Méloné Nyoba Tchonkeu, Soulaimane Berkane, Tarek Hamel. This paper investigates the problem of attitude and air velocity estimation for fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using IMU measurements and at least one Pitot tube measurement, with almost global asymptotic stability (AGAS) guarantees. A cascade observer architecture is developed, in which a Riccati/Kalman-type filter estimates the body-fixed frame air velocity and the vehicle’s tilt using IMU data as inputs and Pitot measurements as outputs.

Emerging evidence points to a critical role for the innate immune system, and several studies had documented concurrent impairment in neutrophil chemot

pmc-10709653.title: Norepinephrine regulates calcium signals and fate of oligodendrocyte precursor cells in the mouse cerebral cortex
pmc-10709653.creator: Frederic Fiore, Khaleel Alhalaseh, Ram R. Dereddi, Felipe Bodaleo Torres, Ilknur Çoban, Ali Harb, Amit Agarwal
pmc-10709653.description: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) generate oligodendrocytes, contributing to myelination and myelin repair. OPCs contact axons and respond to neuronal activity, but how the information relayed by the neuronal activity translates into OPC Ca2+ signals, which in turn influence their fate, remains unknown.

pmc-11413210.title: SPRR1B+ keratinocytes prime oral mucosa for rapid wound healing via STAT3 activation
pmc-11413210.creator: Xinyang Xuanyuan, Li Zhang, Yang Zheng, Ruixin Jiang, Yanni Ma, Ruixin Liu, Pengcong Hou, Ming Lei, Hui Xu, Hanlin Zeng
pmc-11413210.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Oral mucosal wounds exhibit accelerated healing with reduced scarring compared to cutaneous wounds, representing an optimal wound healing paradigm. However, the specific cellular subtypes orchestrating the efficient healing of mucosal tissues remain elusive. Through a comprehensive analysis integrating bulk-mRNA and single-cell sequencing data during the wound healing process in oral mucosa and skin, we have delineated a distinct set of genes markedly upregulated during tissue repair.

pmc-11442133.title: Metabolic activities of marine ammonia‐oxidizing archaea orchestrated by quorum sensing
pmc-11442133.creator: Olivier Pereira, Wei Qin, Pierre E Galand, Didier Debroas, Raphael Lami, Corentin Hochart, Yangkai Zhou, Jin Zhou, Chuanlun Zhang
pmc-11442133.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Ammonia‐oxidizing archaea (AOA) play crucial roles in marine carbon and nitrogen cycles by fixing inorganic carbon and performing the initial step of nitrification. Evaluation of carbon and nitrogen metabolism popularly relies on functional genes such as amoA and accA. Increasing studies suggest that quorum sensing (QS) mainly studied in biofilms for bacteria may serve as a universal communication and regulatory mechanism among prokaryotes; however, this has yet to be demonstrated in marine planktonic archaea.

pmc-11503263.title: Comparison of Measurements for Recording Postural Control in Standing and Seated Position in Healthy Individuals
pmc-11503263.creator: Philipp Floessel, Franziska Hammerschmidt, Jan Jens Koltermann, Justin Foerster, Heidrun Beck, Alexander Carl Disch, Thomas Datzmann
pmc-11503263.description: Background: A standard method of assessing postural control is to measure while standing. However, its implementation is usually limited. Recording postural control directly on the trunk in a seated position could provide an alternative diagnostic method for quantifying neuromuscular control.

pmc-11690972.title: EFFECTS OF CIRCADIAN MISALIGNMENT ON BEHAVIOR IN MAPT HUMANIZED MOUSE MODEL

Circadian misalignment has been found to be related to many neurodegenerative diseases, one of them being Alzheimer’s Disease. Tauopathies, are a distinctive feature of Alzheimer’s Disease and other dementia related disorders.

pmc-12700454.title: Identification of sporulation genes in Bacillus anthracis highlights similarities and significant differences with Bacillus subtilis
pmc-12700454.creator: Fernando H. Ramírez-Guadiana, Anna P. Brogan, Yuanchen Yu, Caroline Midonet, Joel W. Sher, Ernst W. Schmid, Ian J. Roney, David Z. Rudner, Melissa Vazquez Hernandez, Melissa Vazquez Hernandez, Melissa Vazquez Hernandez
pmc-12700454.description: The molecular basis of endospore formation in the model gram-positive bacterium Bacillus subtilis has been investigated for over half a century. Here, using high throughput and classical genetic approaches, we performed a comparative analysis of sporulation in the human pathogen Bacillus anthracis. A transposon-sequencing screen identified >150 genes required for B. anthracis sporulation.

pmc-12705732.title: Emergent scattering regimes in disordered metasurfaces near critical packing
pmc-12705732.creator: M. Chen, A. Agreda, T. Wu, F. Carcenac, K. Vynck, P. Lalanne
pmc-12705732.description: Disordered metasurfaces provide a versatile platform for harnessing near- and far-field scattered light. Most research has focused on either particulate topologies composed of individual, well-identified metaatoms or, to a lesser extent, semi-continuous aggregate topologies without well identified inclusions. Here, we uncover an intermediate ‘critical packing’ regime characterized by metasurface morphologies in which a significant fraction of metaatoms begin to connect.

pmc-12854388.title: Blistering Bulbs: The Hidden Dangers of Garlic as a Home Remedy
pmc-12854388.creator: Riley Bunstine, Christopher M Lloyd
pmc-12854388.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). We report a case of a 46-year-old male who developed a second-degree chemical burn after application of crushed raw garlic to his left wrist. When crushed, garlic activates the enzyme alliinase that converts alliin into allicin. In controlled concentrations, allicin has been shown to have a wide array of therapeutic benefits; however, its use as an unregulated home remedy carries a significant risk of toxicity.

pmc-13183492.title: Incidence of Second Malignancies Among Children Treated for Cancer With Radiotherapy in Egypt
pmc-13183492.creator: Charlotte L Sackett, Mohamed S Zaghloul, Ahmed Aldesouky, Alaa Elhaddad, Li Zhang, Chloe A Teasdale, Amr S Soliman
pmc-13183492.description: BackgroundSurvivors of childhood cancer (CCS) are at risk for secondary malignant neoplasms (SMNs): serious late effects of treatment. Radiotherapy (RT) and chemotherapy (CT) are possible causes of SMNs.AimsTo measure SMN incidence and characteristics among Egyptian CCS treated with RT, and to compare SMN timing and location based on RT field and CT type.

pmc-13589469.title: A large language model-driven multidisciplinary AI agent system predicts delirium in emergency critically ill patients
pmc-13589469.creator: Wen Shang, Tongyue Shi, Qingbian Ma, Guilan Kong
pmc-13589469.description: SummaryDelirium occurs frequently in emergency departments and is associated with poor outcomes and increased burden. Early delirium risk prediction is crucial for timely prevention and intervention in emergency care, but most existing models focus on intensive care unit (ICU) populations and offer limited interpretability and interactivity.

pmc-13656947.title: “It’s Not Like My Old Life, But It’s Still Freedom”: An ACTION learning network mixed methods analysis of the adolescent ventricular assist device experience at home
pmc-13656947.creator: Kelly E Rea, Eleanor Greiner, Katie Flaspohler, Mary C Jenkins, Dean S Karahalios, Michelle Mijon, Shannon Oliver, Zachary Hutchinson, Anna Joong, Joseph Spinner, Melissa K Cousino

Little is known about adolescent and young adult (AYA) experiences during this unique time. This study aims to further understand AYA VAD experience to improve supports and interventions upon discharge.
